subject: How to load a BC1HD crosstype with qtl::read.cross()

messages.author: a2287a1bd46ca727
messages.subject: How to load a BC1HD crosstype with qtl::read.cross()
parts:
Hello,

I'm interested in several populations, originating from different design, always one backcross followed by 5 to 8 selfing, or by an haplodiploidization. To load these data with read.cross(), I simply use BC.gen=1 and F.gen=5 to 8, for the first case. But for the BC1HD design, I was wondering what would be the proper, or at least the better, way to load this crosstype ?

Thanks

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How to load a BC1HD crosstype with qtl::read.cross()
parts:
R/qtl doesn’t have a cross type specific to that design. 

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How to load a BC1HD crosstype with qtl::read.cross()
parts:
The cross type defines
(a) the possible genotypes
(b) the frequency of exchange between markers, and
(c) the relative frequency of the genotypes
which are then used to calculate the probability of each possible genotype in each individual at each position in the genome.

In a BC1DH population, you'd have a skewing of genotypes from 1:1 in a regular DH plus a greater density of crossovers, but if the genotypes are dense and complete, the model for the (b) frequency of exchanges and (c) relative frequency of genotypes wouldn't have much influence.

karl
